observation.visible_scene: A twilight sky scene: a smooth vertical color gradient from pale violet/pink near the bottom horizon to deep blue-purple at the top, overlaid with faint greenish-white aurora structures — a broad ring/arc of light across the upper frame, a diffuse horizontal band through the middle, and several soft vertical ray-like columns hanging down on the right-of-center. A single small bright point (star-like dot) sits near the center. The right edge and lower-right corner are occupied by a static black silhouette of leafy tree branches and the sloped edge of a roof. The framing and the silhouette stay fixed throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The overall composition is essentially static: the tree/roof silhouette, the roofline slope, and the small central bright point hold the same pixel positions from the first to the last frame, indicating no noticeable camera pan, tilt, or zoom.

The aurora glow undergoes only very slow, subtle changes in brightness and soft shape within the excerpt: the greenish rim of the upper ring and the vertical ray columns on the right appear to flicker/shift in intensity slightly from frame to frame, with the right-side vertical band looking marginally more defined toward the later frames.

No object translates across the sky, no aurora band expands into a new region, and no structure appears or disappears; the visible process is a gentle, ongoing luminance/edge fluctuation of already-present auroral light rather than a start or stop of motion.
The sky gradient and horizon tint remain constant in color and position, so the only real change is the faint internal shimmer of the aurora.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the aurora is brightening, dimming, or drifting overall beyond this short window (the excerpt shows no clear trend, only micro-fluctuations).
The cause of the auroral light and the identity of the small bright point (star vs. planet) are not established by the frames.
What lies outside the right frame and below the horizon, and whether the silhouette moves in wind, is not shown.
uncertain_details: The frame-to-frame differences in the aurora are small enough that some could be compression noise or exposure variation rather than true physical motion; the apparent slight brightening of the right vertical ray is not definitive.
Camera motion is judged as negligible based on the fixed silhouette and star, but cannot be entirely ruled out at sub-pixel scale.
The exact geometry of the aurora (ring vs. arc vs. corona) is ambiguous due to the diffuse, low-contrast glow.

the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.

do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.

properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;

and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
